statement: Writing a value to allocation/<bg-type>/bg_reclaim_threshold stores it in the space info after a 0 to 100 range check, so a value outside that range returns EINVAL and leaves the threshold unchanged.

The value read from allocation/<bg-type>/bg_reclaim_threshold comes from btrfs_calc_reclaim_threshold under the space-info lock instead of the stored field, so what sysfs prints is a computed threshold.

Read /sys/fs/btrfs/<UUID>/bg_reclaim_threshold for the filesystem-wide block-group reclaim threshold; outside a debug build the write accepts only 0 or 51 through 100 and rejects 1 through 50 with EINVAL.
The allocation directory holds global_rsv_reserved as well as global_rsv_size, and both pointers are registered in one attribute group, so the pair exists for every mounted filesystem.
global_rsv_size in the allocation directory reports the global block reserve's size as a decimal unsigned integer, emitted from the block reserve's size field under its lock.
